license: Original schematic illustrations for this repository. No measured performance is implied.

diagrams.title: From words to ranked documents
rows: Tokenize and normalize documents and queries.
Find documents sharing analyzed query terms.
Combine IDF, saturating term frequency and length.
Scores rank matches; they are not probabilities.
diagrams.note: Lexical overlap and semantic similarity are complementary signals.

diagrams.title: Chunk boundaries change the evidence
rows: Keep headings, source IDs and document boundaries.
Balance complete meaning against context length.
Use the same chunking revision in the evaluation.
Check evidence coverage, noise and context cost.
diagrams.note: Overlap can protect boundaries, but also introduces duplicate evidence.

diagrams.title: DiskANN: compact routing, SSD graph
rows: Compare against compact PQ codes and cached nodes.
A graph traversal selects what to read next.
Read graph neighbors and full vectors as needed.
Return neighbors under the chosen search budget.
diagrams.note: Measure recall, memory and cold / warm tail latency together.

diagrams.title: mmap and DiskANN act at different layers
rows: Local cache and eviction are separate.
diagrams.note: A mapped file still consumes physical memory when its pages are resident.

diagrams.title: CAGRA uses parallel GPU graph search
rows: Choose graph degree and build configuration.
Search width and pool size trade work for recall.
Include batches, transfers and GPU memory.
diagrams.note: A GPU needs enough useful work; compare at the same recall target.

diagrams.title: Choose the index by the binding constraint
rows: Cost grows with the searched data.
Budget for both vectors and graph.
Trade memory for local SSD I/O.
diagrams.note: These are candidates to benchmark, not universal performance rankings.

diagrams.title: Library, index layer and database
rows: Use SDKs to write, filter and search collections.
Owns schemas, distributed serving and lifecycle.
Provides the vector-index abstraction and integration.
FAISS and other engines supply search algorithms.
diagrams.note: An ANN library supplies algorithms; a database adds operational semantics.

diagrams.title: Range search adds a score condition
rows: Apply the chosen metric, index and filters.
ANN search may miss qualifying neighbors.
A full result may be truncated; it is not a census.
diagrams.note: For COSINE / IP the band is radius < score <= range_filter.

diagrams.title: Retrieve broadly, rerank a shortlist
rows: Dense, lexical or hybrid search finds a pool.
A reranker reads each query-document pair.
Keep the best evidence within the context budget.
Measure relevance, answer quality and added latency.
diagrams.note: A reranker cannot recover a document absent from its candidate pool.

diagrams.title: Diagnose a recall plateau step by step
rows: Use the same corpus, metric, normalization and filter.
Hold graph build settings and workload constant.
If needed, test quantizer precision and connectivity.
diagrams.note: The shape of a recall curve alone does not identify the cause.

diagrams.title: Application clusters are explicit labels
rows: Use Spark or a bounded data-export workflow.
Fit k-means, HDBSCAN or another chosen method.
Keep record ID, cluster_id and algorithm revision.
Filter, sample or analyze application groups.
diagrams.note: Internal IVF centroid assignments are not application cluster IDs.

diagrams.title: Similarity proposes a duplicate; rules decide
rows: Use scope, hashes and stable source identifiers.
Dense search or MinHash supplies possible pairs.
Check thresholds, content and task-specific evidence.
Keep provenance and an explicit survivor policy.
diagrams.note: Approximate similarity is candidate generation, not proof of identity.

diagrams.title: Mine difficult non-matches, then verify
rows: Keep development and final test data separate.
Find high-scoring candidates that look relevant.
Remove unlabeled positives and ambiguous cases.
Version the mining setup and inspect regressions.
diagrams.note: A highly ranked unlabeled document is not automatically a negative.

diagrams.title: Select useful variety, not only distant points
rows: Enforce rights, quality, version and safety scope.
Treat capped ANN results as incomplete evidence.
Balance task strata, relevance and diversity.
Keep IDs, criteria and a versioned manifest.
diagrams.note: Outliers may be corrupt data; distance alone does not establish value.

diagrams.title: Quality gates before the vector index
rows: Check rights, stable IDs, freshness and completeness.
Check model version, dimensions and finite values.
Enforce tenant, timestamps and filterable field types.
Test queries, labels and failure slices before release.
diagrams.note: A faster index does not repair an incorrect or stale representation.

diagrams.title: Two required signals need two explicit checks
rows: Intersect or verify the same pair.
diagrams.note: Rank fusion alone does not enforce a visual AND text threshold.

diagrams.title: Join by stable identity, not file position
diagrams.note: Keep a versioned mapping so refresh, deletion and replay remain traceable.

diagrams.title: Deletion must reach every derived copy
rows: Keep stable IDs and a durable event or tombstone.
Delete or exclude all corresponding search rows.
Apply policy to exports, caches and other replicas.
Track replay progress and test that content is absent.
diagrams.note: A curation exclusion and an erasure request have different semantics.

diagrams.title: File formats and table layers solve different jobs
rows: Moves typed data between compute stages.
Tracks schema, files and table versions.
diagrams.note: Choose an integration against its documented version and capabilities.

diagrams.title: Storage readers follow a committed manifest
rows: Persist columnar data in the supported storage layout.
Record the visible files and version metadata.
Resolve logical rows through the committed state.
diagrams.note: milvus-storage is a storage layer; Knowhere serves vector-index algorithms.

diagrams.title: Reproduce the experiment, not just the data
rows: Pin lake and collection versions; retain the files.
Pin model revision, preprocessing and chunk boundaries.
Pin index settings, queries, labels and metric code.
Pin software and hardware; repeat and record variance.
diagrams.note: A data snapshot alone does not guarantee identical ANN result order.

diagrams.title: Separate remote storage from the hot working set
rows: Hot index structures, cached pages and query execution.
Larger indexes, fetched chunks and mapped field files.
Durable source data, snapshots and cold objects.
Warm up, fetch and evict according to the workload.
diagrams.note: Benchmark cold starts and shifted traffic, not only a warm cache.

diagrams.title: Vector bytes are only one part of memory
rows: Count x dimension x bytes, or compressed code size.
Add graph links, centroids, IDs and scalar fields.
Include the actual shard and replica placement.
Budget for queries, ingestion, caches and maintenance.
diagrams.note: Payload compression ratios are not whole-service memory reductions.

diagrams.title: Eligibility comes before memory ranking
rows: Keep source, tenant, time, version and memory type.
Exclude expired, deleted and superseded facts.
Normalize score direction before blending signals.
Update current state; preserve decision history separately.
diagrams.note: Down-ranking an obsolete fact is not the same as making it ineligible.

diagrams.title: Agent memory has different jobs and owners
rows: Keep a bounded prompt or explicit state store.
diagrams.note: One vector collection does not replace every state or persistence mechanism.

diagrams.title: Reuse applicable experience, not raw traces
rows: Store ordered steps, tool results and outcome.
Embed task, summary or selected step windows.
Match tenant, tools, environment and applicability.
Verify and summarize before giving it to the agent.
diagrams.note: Similarity proposes experience; context and outcome determine usefulness.

diagrams.title: A training example needs an explicit selection rule
rows: Pin policy, task, environment and outcome evidence.
Protect evaluation tasks and dataset boundaries.
SFT successes or task-matched preference pairs.
Keep selected IDs, reasons, versions and coverage.
diagrams.note: Reward is a quality signal; embeddings help with similarity and coverage.

diagrams.title: A similar question is not enough for a cache hit
rows: Match tenant, permissions, model and source version.
Use a calibrated threshold for the task.
Reject expired or invalidated evidence and answers.
Reuse only if every validity condition passes.
diagrams.note: Measure false hits and stale answers, not only cache-hit rate.

diagrams.title: Graph and vector retrieval supply different evidence
rows: Evaluate against an ordinary RAG baseline.
diagrams.note: Milvus stores searchable representations; graph traversal needs its own layer.

diagrams.title: Coding agents need lexical and semantic evidence
rows: Keep paths, symbols, language and commit IDs.
Use grep / exact lookup for names and identifiers.
Use embeddings for behavior and intent.
Read definitions, callers and current source.
diagrams.note: Vector similarity complements exact code search; it does not prove behavior.

diagrams.title: Framework orchestration and vector storage
rows: Defines the task, access scope and expected outcome.
Loads data, calls models and orchestrates retrieval.
Stores vectors and metadata; filters and retrieves.
Assembles evidence and evaluates the final output.
diagrams.note: Framework state, checkpoints and model inference have separate owners.

diagrams.title: Optimize a program on a development set
rows: Choose signatures, tools and the Milvus retriever.
Specify a metric and representative questions.
Tune the program while holding data versions fixed.
Use held-out examples and inspect failure slices.
diagrams.note: An optimizer changes application behavior; it does not replace the database.

diagrams.title: A benchmark score needs its evaluation contract
rows: Check modality, language, dataset and metric.
Do not mix protocols or assume equal coverage.
Measure relevance, latency, cost and operating limits.
diagrams.note: MTEB and MMEB summarize tasks; neither guarantees production suitability.

diagrams.title: Shortlist models by the workload
diagrams.note: Keep model revisions separate; equal dimensions do not mean equal spaces.

diagrams.title: Three places to generate a representation
rows: Does not imply arbitrary model support.
diagrams.note: A wrapper export is not proof of executed inference or universal compatibility.

diagrams.title: Choose the operational responsibility boundary
rows: Service runs in your cloud account
Clarify network, IAM and shared duties.
Validate the support and compliance scope.
diagrams.note: Account ownership alone does not describe every operational responsibility.

diagrams.title: Compare total cost at a matched service target
rows: Compute, RAM, SSD, replicas and required headroom.
Object storage, requests, networking and backups.
Embedding inference, refresh jobs and reranking.
Engineering, on-call, upgrades, recovery and support.
diagrams.note: Match recall, latency, availability and workload before comparing prices.

diagrams.title: A backup is useful when a restore succeeds
rows: Choose acceptable data loss and recovery time.
Back up data, metadata and configuration safely.
Check IDs, counts, indexes, filters and query behavior.
Record timing, replay steps and rollback evidence.
diagrams.note: Replication, CDC, snapshots and backup solve different recovery problems.

diagrams.title: A deployment is verified by a working query
rows: Pin server and SDK versions; verify the endpoint.
Use stable IDs and a known embedding contract.
Apply the chosen index, metric and filter.
Read known rows and compare expected neighbors.
diagrams.note: A running process alone does not prove a usable retrieval workflow.

diagrams.title: Authorization and retrieval filters are separate
rows: Establish an identity at the service boundary.
Use RBAC and service-side permission checks.
Return only authorized evidence and record access.
diagrams.note: An untrusted caller-supplied tenant filter is not an access-control boundary.

diagrams.title: Shards divide data; replicas copy serving capacity
rows: Adds another part of the corpus.
Has one set of serving copies.
Uses additional resources for availability / load.
diagrams.note: More shards and more replicas have different resource and routing costs.

diagrams.title: Scale the stage that limits the workload
rows: Separate routing, filtering, search and payload I/O.
Check CPU, memory, SSD, GPU, queues and network.
Adjust index, shards, replicas or ingestion capacity.
Include writes, failures, cold caches and skew.
diagrams.note: Vector count alone does not determine useful throughput or latency.

diagrams.title: Use Attu to inspect a reproducible retrieval case
rows: Check schema, indexes, loaded state and row metadata.
Keep the vector, filter and search parameters.
Use the same case in a reproducible script.
diagrams.note: A UI inspection complements metrics and logs; it does not replace them.

diagrams.title: MinHash approximates set overlap
rows: Represent each document as a set of text fragments.
Use the same hashing and signature configuration.
Compare signatures under the supported metric.
Check content overlap and an explicit decision threshold.
diagrams.note: This is lexical set similarity, not a dense semantic embedding.

diagrams.title: Sparse neighborhoods flag candidates for review
rows: Use the same metric, filters and data version.
kNN distances or capped range hits provide signals.
ANN misses can change the apparent local density.
Separate novelty, corruption and real incidents.
diagrams.note: A capped range-search count is a lower bound, not a complete density.

diagrams.title: Refresh is a small data release
rows: Finish the source write and record the snapshot or version.
Keep the job ID; wait for completion and handle failures.
Inspect indexes and verify added, changed and deleted IDs.
Measure source commit to validated search results.
diagrams.note: An accepted refresh request does not prove that the new data is searchable.
